newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Thursday and traders said a plunge on the domestic A share markets was the major factor pulling down the rates.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract closed unchanged at 16.00 percent.
Total turnover rose sharply to 13.09 million lots from 6.57 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The fall of the A share markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen depressed sentiment on the repo market, with institutions selling heavily," said one trader.
Traders believe the rates will continue to fall on Friday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed, with investor confidence very weak because contracts have been on a downward trend for months, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, fell to 116.09 yuan from 116.61 yuan on institutional selling, they said.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market rose slightly to 1.08 million lots from 1.00 million.
Traders said they were not optimistic about the short-term trend. -- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
